I am Dean Martin, representing the Guelph Accessibility Advisory Committee as the Vice
Chair.
Working with the City and staff, we have come up with three motions in regards to the traffic
calming policy, which I will refer to as TCP.
The first motion that we had come up with is that the ACC receives the presentation from
the TCP update, which we did, and that the ACC endorsed the following recommendations
to the TCP as proposed by the engineering and transportation services.
The first recommendation is TCP will incorporate the most effective traffic calming measures
for reducing vehicle speeds, which may include the use and recommended spacing of raised
crossings and speed cushions.
The TCP will be evidence-informed and data-driven by prioritizing the proactive installation
of traffic calming measures in the community safety zones.
Third recommendation, TCP will prioritize addressing the streets with the highest risk
of collision-related injuries over the first-come, first-served approach.
The fourth recommendation of the first motion is the TCP will add new traffic calming measures
to align with the City's complete street design guidelines, the latest traffic calming
approaches and incorporate measures which encourage active transportation.
The second motion that we put forward is that the ACC provide the following comments as
it relates to recommendations to the TCP for staff consideration.
TCP will consider greater focus on horizontal measures such as road narrowing.
Vertical measures such as cushions should not be the default solution for traffic calming in the TCP.
TCP will consider the...
Sorry, new glasses.
We will consider pedestrian measures such as tactile walking indicators and contrasting
lines and follow Canadian National Institute for the Blind guidelines.
Also that the TCP emphasized winter maintenance of pedestrian measures.
And that the TCP allows for measures that clarify cyclist, pedestrian, and driver prioritization.
And the final motion that we put forward is that the ACC recommend that staff request returning to the ACC as part of the TCP review in 2026.
